title: quest init prints the literal word 'undefined' for optional fields it never selected
description:
Reported by the user via opum-agent, running `quest init` in a fresh project (name cometx, prefix ctx). --plain output:

  configuration:
    agentSkillSource: undefined
    name: cometx
    taskIdPrefix: ctx
  instructions:
    state: current
  instructionsByTarget: undefined
  skill:
    state: current

Reproduced 2026-09-12 in a scratch workspace with the exact scripted flags:
`quest init --name cometx --task-id-prefix ctx --agent-instructions --target claude --plain` -- byte-identical shape.

TRIAGE, per the request to distinguish display-only from data-loss: this is display-only. Confirmed by running the SAME init with --json instead of --plain: both fields are absent from the envelope entirely, and the write each represents happened correctly --  `instructions.state` is populated (the single-target write path ran) and the workspace/skill writes succeeded. Nothing is being dropped; a caller reading --json has always gotten the correct, quiet omission. The bug is confined to the human renderer.

ROOT CAUSE, isolated to one line: src/cli/render.ts:61, `renderScalar`: `if (value === undefined) return "undefined";`. `Object.entries()` on a plain object literal keeps keys whose value is JS `undefined` (confirmed: `Object.entries({a:1,b:undefined})` -> `[['a',1],['b',undefined]]`), while `JSON.stringify` drops them (`JSON.stringify({a:1,b:undefined})` -> `'{"a":1}'`). `renderHumanPayload`'s own doc comment already commits to matching JSON's collection conventions for empty arrays/objects; an undefined-valued key is the same class of asymmetry and the renderer chose the opposite of that convention for it.

BLAST RADIUS: today, only `quest init`'s `workspace.initialized`/`workspace.reconfigured` payload builds a data object this way (src/cli/main.ts:1017-1022, spreading `instructions`, `instructionsByTarget`, `agentSkillSource` in unconditionally rather than via a conditional spread). Every other surface checked (`task view`, `task list`) constructs its payload so optional fields are omitted before reaching the renderer, which is why this has not been seen elsewhere. But the defect is in the shared renderer, not the init command, so it will recur at the next command that follows the same natural pattern of assigning an optional variable straight into an object literal. Fixing render.ts protects every current and future call site; fixing only `quest init`'s object construction would not.

FIX: filter entries whose value is `undefined` out of the object-rendering path in `renderLines` before sorting/rendering, matching `JSON.stringify`'s behavior -- an object left with zero entries after filtering renders `{}`, consistent with the existing empty-object convention. Leave `renderScalar`'s own `undefined` branch as the fallback for a genuinely top-level undefined payload (unreachable today, but a reasonable rendering if it ever is).

finalSummary:
quest init --plain no longer prints the literal word 'undefined' for a field it never selected (agentSkillSource, instructionsByTarget). Confirmed display-only, not data loss, before fixing: the identical --json invocation always omitted both keys correctly, and the underlying writes were correct.

Root cause: src/cli/render.ts's object renderer used Object.entries(), which keeps a key whose value is JS undefined -- unlike JSON.stringify, which drops it -- and renderScalar explicitly rendered that undefined as the literal string. Fixed by filtering undefined-valued entries out before the emptiness check in renderLines, so the human renderer now matches JSON's own semantics and the renderer's existing empty-object {} convention. Scoped to the shared renderer, not quest init's object construction, since the defect was in the renderer and protects every current and future command that assigns an optional field straight into a data object.

Verified: quest init --name cometx --task-id-prefix ctx --agent-instructions --target claude --plain and the same for --reconfigure --plain, both manually reproduced pre-fix and confirmed clean post-fix. Two new/extended tests: a render.ts unit test asserting an undefined-valued key (top-level and nested) is omitted rather than printed, and an end-to-end CLI-process test reproducing the exact scripted quest init repro and asserting --json is unaffected. npm run check exits 0 -- 456 tests, 0 fail; the one pre-existing lint warning in test/qcli122-fourth-pass.test.ts is unrelated and untouched.
